assembly_info.comments:
Background: Leishmania sp. MAR, or Martinique, LEM2494 (MHOM/MQ/92/MAR1) was obtained from Professeurs Jean-Pierre Dedet and Patrick Bastien, University Montepellier, France. This parasite was isolated from a skin lesion of a human patient exhibiting diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis and infected with HIV. H. Noyes, F. Pratlong, M. Chance, J. Ellis, G. Lanotte & J-P. Dedet (2002), A previously unclassified trypanosomatid responsible for human cutaneous lesions in Martinique (French West Indies) is the most divergent member of the genus Leishmania, Parasitology (2002), 124, 17-24; J-P. Dedet, B. Roche, F. Pratlong, D. Cales-Quist, J. Jouannelle, J.C. Benichou & M. Huerre (1995), Diffuse cutaneous infection caused by a presumed monoxenous trypanosomatid in a patient infected with HIV, Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene 89:644-646. Genomic DNA was prepared from nuclei isolated from parasites lysed using 0.5% NP-40, to minimize the amount of kinetoplast (mitochondrial) DNA, and was provided by Drs. Deborah E Dobson and Stephen M. Beverley, Washington University School of Medicine. Total sequence coverage of Illumina instrument reads was 187X (fragments, 3 and 8kb) using a genome size estimate of 35Mb. The combined sequence reads were assembled using the ALLPATHS software (Broad Institute). This draft assembly was referred to as Leishmania sp. MAR LEM2494 1.0.3. This version has been gap filled and cleaned of contaminating contigs. The assembly is made up of a total of 337 scaffolds with an N50 scaffold length of over 489kb (N50 contig length was 147kb). The assembly spans 30.5Mb. This work was supported by NIH grant AI29646 to SMB and by NIH-NHGRI grant 5U54HG00307907 to RKW, Director of The Genome Institute at Washington University. For questions regarding this Leishmania sp. MAR LEM2494 1.0.2 assembly please contact Dr. Wesley Warren, Washington University School of Medicine (wwarren@genome.wustl.edu). Downloads of the sequence data are available via the TriTrypDB genome browser server. Funding for the sequence characterization of the Leishmania MAR LEM2494 genome was provided by the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH).
